about_the_game:
Subtle Changes

Slight changes done by something or someone occur to make you have an underlying sense of something being out of place.

Claustrophobic Tools

It's Bad Enough the news station borrowed this camera from your grandma, but while snapping photos, changing lenses and cleaning the camera your vision is very limited, and while your mind focuses on the menial tasks, glitches start to occur, your weather reader encounters an error that forces you to venture into the ice cold backyard with only one exit, all this while you hear a knock on the window, it's too late...

Shaping Your Fate With Dialogue Branches

The locals vary from informative, outcasts, sinister and worst of all, normal with an underlying sense of something deeply wrong. These individuals shape your fate and how much you uncover or don't uncover.

Environmental Storytelling

The residents aren't the only thing burying secrets, the environment itself seems to warp, shift, breathe. With rolling fog, jagged cliff-sides, low-cawing gulls and a symbol that seems to be everywhere.

Advanced Video Settings

The stunning environment of Grim Fate can be explored with video settings suited for your hardware. Lower settings provide better performance for older hardware, medium settings offer our polished default experience, and higher settings deliver enhanced graphical fidelity, alongside adjustable framerate targets to suit your preferences.

Masterfully Crafted SFX And Soundtrack

SFX Shape the game's atmospheric terror and make it almost too real, this is very much the case in Grim Fate with subtle hints and changes that make you want to stop and listen, but are scared whatever it is might catch up...

"Mists Of The Unknown" Is a special track heard in the moor biome, it's a simple ambience track with low cinematic drones as a foundation and haunting ghost notes that are eerily beautiful and add another element of foreshadowing and mystery, much like the rest of the impressive 14 song soundtrack.

Accessibility Features For Everyone Wanting To Experience The Horrors

Cloverleaf Bay may be unforgiving, but has a wide variety of accessibility features for those who are colourblind, prefer different key binds, those who prefer a larger text size, and many more so everyone can enjoy Grim Fate in their own way.

Breadcrumbs Of The Story

  • An old man warned you. Was it just a local eccentric, or something darker?

  • The faint whispers you hear... are they real, or your mind cracking under pressure? 

  • Your phone is gone. Was it lost, or taken?

  • The more you explore, the more you'll find that Cloverleaf Bay has secrets it's desperate to keep buried.

As you dig deeper into the town's twisted past, you'll uncover a nightmare that grows ever closer. Will you survive the night, or become another lost soul to the bay?

content_descriptors.notes: Grim Fate displays topics including criminal organizations, manipulative and controlling individuals, frightening horror elements including psychological horror, non-violent death scenes, and survivor's guilt.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS *: Windows 7 64 Bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i3-6100 / AMD FX-6300
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 750 Ti / AMD Radeon R7 260X
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
  • Sound Card: DirectX Compatible
  • Additional Notes: Headphones recommended for optimal audio experience

Recommended:

  • Sound Card: DirectX Compatible

short_description: Immerse yourself in a polished VHS style psychological horror experience, with an atmospheric first person view, branching dialogues, environmental clues, a mystery to uncover and some things that aren't quite right that will keep you questioning what's real and what's not.
supported_languages:
English*, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese
*languages with full audio support
